newsitem.title: USA: L.A. mayor backs $615 mln police, library bonds.
newsitem.headline: L.A. mayor backs $615 mln police, library bonds.

text.p: Los Angeles Mayor Richard Riordan has vowed to support ballot measures that would raise more than $615 million for police and library projects as part his proposed $4 billion spending plan for 1997-98.

The mayor told the Los Angeles City Council in a letter that he would support a $465 million bond issue for police and fire facilities as well as a $150 million bond for library improvements. The letter was presented the city council on Friday.
The general obligation bond measures could appear on the June 1998 ballot, city officials said.
Riordan, who was re-elected as leader of the second-largest U.S. city earlier this month, announced his support for the bonds as part of his 1997-98 budget package.
The mayor's $4 billion spending plan -- $50 million smaller than last year's -- would contain a reserve of $30 million and involve 470 job cuts. The budget seeks no new taxes.
The budget would rely less on one-time funds to cut the city's structural deficit. With these changes, Riordan's office has forecast a small surplus in five years.
The full Los Angeles City Council is expected to begin debating the mayor's budget plan on May 19.
On Monday, Los Angeles County's chief administrative officer plans to unveil his budget plan for the county. The county's 1996-97 budget topped $12 billion.
